UNCALIBRATED: tracking mode until at least 50 first-ENTER coins are graded with a no-data share of 20% or less (a minimum sample, not a calibration)

stats.peakSampling: peaks sampled at each momentum refresh of a tracked coin (about every 75 s with 27 tracked) and by the grader every 10 min (oldest 60 open rows per pass) once a coin is no longer tracked: spikes between samples are missed, so HIT_5M and DOUBLED are lower bounds

graded.note: buy at the signal, sell when the row was graded (HIT_5M at the first sample at or above the target, RUGGED at rug detection, otherwise at the horizon); $100 per signal, net of pool fees and impact on both legs at the liquidity that existed at each; 0 of a 50-signal minimum: counts only, no claim of edge

hold.note: buy at the signal, sell at the 72 h horizon mark whatever happened in between (the replicable rule; a rugged pool is -100); $100 per signal, net of pool fees and impact on both legs at the liquidity that existed at each; 0 of a 50-signal minimum: counts only, no claim of edge

peak.note: sell at the sampled peak (a ceiling, not an achievable exit); $100 per signal, net of pool fees and impact on both legs, the exit priced at the liquidity recorded at the peak, or the entry pool's depth for rows older than that recording (the ceiling is understated when depth grew with price); 0 of a 50-signal minimum: counts only, no claim of edge

expectancy.basis: first ENTER signal per coin, graded rows only; entry at the signal's liquidity; pool fees and impact on both legs. graded: exit at the liquidity the grader saw when it closed the row (HIT_5M rows at the target sample, a limit-sell-at-target, not a hold to the horizon). hold: exit at the 72 h horizon mark, recorded for every row detected since 2026-10-20 within a day of its horizon (older or unpriced rows are skipped; a rugged pool is -100 under every rule). peak: the sampled peak at its own recorded liquidity, or the entry depth for rows older than the recording. Market-cap multiples stand in for price multiples, which overstates the move when supply grew
